examples.ja: すみません、駅はどこですか。
examples.romaji: sumimasen, eki wa doko desu ka.
examples.en: Excuse me, where is the station?

cards.tip: X wa doko desu ka is the template: X + wa (topic) + doko (where) + desu ka. Swap X for any place.
Same template. toire is from English 'toilet'; otearai is the politer word on signs, with the same o- prefix as omizu.
The ko-so-a-do set: ko- is near me. koko (here), kore (this thing), kono + noun (this X).
so- is near the listener. soko (there), sore (that thing), sono + noun.
a- is away from both of you. asoko (over there), are (that thing over there), ano + noun.

examples.ja: 次の角を右に曲がってください。
examples.romaji: tsugi no kado o migi ni magatte kudasai.
examples.en: Turn right at the next corner.

cards.tip: Noun. Add ni to make it a direction: migi ni (to the right). migigawa = the right side.
Noun, same pattern: hidari ni magatte kudasai, please turn left.

examples.ja: まっすぐ行ってください。

cards.tip: Adverb. The small tsu (っ) is a stop: mas-sugu, not masugu. Hold the pause.
chikai is an i-adjective; i-adjectives take desu directly. Negative: chikakunai desu.
i-adjective with a long o: too-i. A short toi is not a word; the length matters.

cards.ja: この電車は新宿に行きますか
cards.romaji: kono densha wa shinjuku ni ikimasu ka
cards.en: Does this train go to Shinjuku?
cards.tip: kono (this) + densha (train) + wa + place + ni (to, destination particle) + ikimasu (go) + ka. ni marks where you are heading.

cards.ja: どこで乗り換えますか
cards.tip: de marks where an action happens. norikaeru = nori (ride) + kaeru (change).
Noun with a stop: kip-pu. kippu uriba = ticket counter.
kai (open) + satsu (ticket). kaisatsuguchi is the full word for the gate itself, with -guchi (opening).

examples.romaji: higashi deguchi wa doko desu ka.

cards.tip: de (go out, from deru) + guchi (mouth, opening). iriguchi is the entrance, same -guchi.

cards.ja: ここまでお願いします
cards.en: To here, please (showing a taxi driver an address)
cards.tip: made = up to, as far as. koko made = to here. Pair it with a map or written address in a taxi.

cards.ja: ここで止めてください
cards.tip: tomete is the -te form of tomeru (to stop); -te kudasai is the polite 'please do'. Any verb works: matte kudasai, please wait.
nan (what) + ban (number) + sen (line, track). nan + a counter asks 'which' or 'how many'.
basu (bus, loanword) + tei (stop). Loanwords are written in katakana.
aruite (-te form of aruku, walk) + ikemasu (can go, potential of iku). The -te form chains verbs: 'walking, can I go'.
